comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, Citi's total credit exposure to commercial real estate was $65 billion, including $6 billion related to office buildings, with the remainder primarily attributed to corporate clients.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citi disclose their specific credit exposure to the U.S. government and municipal sectors, breaking down the amounts by accounting classification or portfolio type. JPMorgan explicitly details its exposure to U.S. state and municipal governments by categorizing holdings into trading assets, available-for-sale (AFS) securities, and held-to-maturity (HTM) securities. Similarly, Citi provides a granular breakdown of its commercial real estate (CRE) credit exposure, distinguishing between corporate clients and Wealth clients. While the specific asset classes differ (JPM focuses on government securities while Citi focuses on CRE loans in this specific disclosure), both filings serve the same function of quantifying credit exposure to major public sector or real estate-related obligors with specific dollar amounts and year-over-year comparisons.

sentences.text: (c)In addition to the credit risk exposure to states and municipal governments (both U.S. and non-U.S.) at December 31, 2024 and 2023, noted above, the Firm held: $6.1 billion and $5.9 billion, respectively, of trading assets; $17.9 billion and $21.4 billion, respectively, of AFS securities; and $9.3 billion and $9.9 billion, respectively, of HTM securities, issued by U.S. state and municipal governments.

As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, Citi's total credit exposure to commercial real estate (CRE) was $65 billion and $66 billion, including $6 billion and $8 billion of exposure related to office buildings, respectively.
This total CRE exposure consisted of approximately $56 billion and $55 billion, respectively, related to corporate clients, included in the real estate category in the tables above and below.
Total CRE exposure also includes approximately $9 billion and $11 billion, respectively, related to Wealth clients that is not in the tables as they are not considered corporate exposures.
